concerns_addressed: Delivery completion now acquires Order::lockForUpdate inside the same transaction before Delivery::transitionTo and Order::recordStatus('Delivered'), so the order row, order status, and order history mutation use the locked instance (apps/api/app/Http/Controllers/DeliveryController.php:114-127).

The concurrent regression uses two independent public HTTP workers and an opt-in barrier reached by both delivery completion and payment before order-row contention; it asserts final order status, order_status_history consistency, exactly one Delivered history entry, and the public tracking response (apps/api/tests/Feature/DeliveryTest.php:154-232).

Sales visit planning, authenticated role scoping, target/date validation, delivery assignment for confirmed orders, active-driver validation, assignment/status mutation scoping, explicit delivery transitions, and delivery status history are implemented and exercised through REST endpoints.

Proof metadata is validated, persisted, returned, and audited; the delivery UI now requires and submits recipient name plus proof URL before allowing completion (apps/api/app/Http/Requests/UpdateDeliveryStatusRequest.php:12-25; apps/web/src/app/delivery/page.tsx:30-55).

Order integration records Delivered and order status history atomically with delivery completion, and focused tests assert both database history and public order tracking history (apps/api/tests/Feature/DeliveryTest.php:108-145).

The original sales and delivery implementation cycles remain separate commits (e5c2b82 and 6341612), with endpoint integration tests for each; the repair commit adds the requested cross-entity regression and proof capture.
Focused T6 tests pass: 6 tests and 47 assertions. The complete API suite passes: 59 tests and 359 assertions. The Next.js production build and workspace TypeScript build both succeed.

strengths: Delivery completion and order status/history writes are enclosed by one transaction, with the related order row locked before either cross-entity mutation.
Delivery::canTransition rejects skipped, repeated, and terminal-state transitions; transition history and proof metadata are written atomically with the delivery update.
Role and ownership checks scope delivery reads and mutations to admins, assigning sales users, and assigned drivers; sales visits are scoped to their sales user.
Assignment locks the order and driver and is backed by a unique deliveries.order_id constraint, preventing duplicate assignments under concurrency.
Routing and calendar integrations remain simple injectable MVP seams with no complex routing algorithm.
Validation and HTTP error handling cover invalid roles, inactive/non-driver assignment, unconfirmed orders, invalid transitions, invalid proof URLs, and unauthorized access.

The concurrent test genuinely overlaps public HTTP transactions at a controlled critical-section barrier and verifies both persistence and tracking API consistency; all API tests and the web build are green.

issues.description: The delivery UI captures recipient name and a proof URL but does not expose the API's optional structured photo/signature fields, so richer proof metadata still requires another client.
